name: Hamrin and the Eastern Gate
inspired_by: The Iraq-Iran borderlands of Diyala and the Zagros foothills as of 2026: a Diyala-type river plain with palm groves and citrus orchards, the Hamrin-type sandstone ridge and reservoir where Islamic State remnant cells still hide, mixed Arab, Kurdish and Turkmen districts disputed between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region, a border crossing on the pilgrim road, and Iranian foothill towns below the first Zagros range (Kermanshah-type) on the east edge. Iran has been at war with the US and Israel since February 2026 (hostilities resumed in September 2026); Iran-aligned Iraqi factions hold stretches of the border economy; US forces left federal Iraq by 30 September 2026. All towns are fictional.
climate: Hot semi-arid (Koppen BSh) on the plain, 45-50 C in July and 4-16 C in January with 250-350 mm of winter rain; the Iranian foothills (Csa) are cooler and wetter (400-500 mm, snow on the range in winter). Frequent summer dust storms; winter fog in the palm groves.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb): rain and fog, green steppe, snow on the Zagros range, muddy tracks
Spring (Mar-May): wheat green then gold, wildflowers on Hamrin, dust storms begin
Summer (Jun-Sep): extreme heat, low reservoir, dust storms, date harvest begins in late summer
Autumn (Oct-Nov): date and citrus harvest; Arbaeen pilgrim traffic peaks at the crossing (date shifts with the lunar calendar)

vegetation: citrus and pomegranate orchards under the palms
reed and tamarisk on canal banks
terraced gardens and walnut by streams

terrain.relief: A flat river plain at 70-150 m in the west; a long, narrow sandstone ridge (Hamrin type) rising to 300-450 m across the centre with a reservoir behind a dam where the river cuts through it; rolling foothill steppe at 200-500 m in the north and east; and the first Zagros range (limestone, 1,200-1,850 m) along the east edge on the Iranian side.
features: palm groves cut by irrigation canals
the Hamrin-type ridge with gullies, caves and old trenches
a river gorge through the ridge
a border crossing and customs zone in a valley
oil wells and a shared oil field straddling the border
old 1980s war berms and trench lines (UXO hazard)
Zagros limestone anticline with oak woodland
terrain.water: A river (Diyala/Sirwan type) crossing the map from the Iranian mountains to the plain, dammed into a reservoir at the ridge; a network of irrigation canals in the plain; seasonal streams in the foothills; wells.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Flat plain with low noise; the Hamrin ridge as an anisotropic ridged stamp along a NW-SE axis with gully erosion; the reservoir as a flood fill behind a dam stamp in the river gap; foothills as low simplex hills; the Zagros front as a folded anticline (sine ridge along NW-SE) with ridged detail. A border line spline runs along the foothills on the east third.

noise_layers.type: folded anticline (sine along NW-SE) plus ridged detail
noise_layers.purpose: Zagros front range on the Iranian side
badland gullies and rills on the ridge
palm grove vs field mask on the plain

generator.erosion: Strong hydraulic erosion on the Hamrin ridge (badlands); thermal erosion on the limestone range; minimal on the plain.
generator.rivers: Main river spline from the east edge through the foothills and the ridge gap into the plain; reservoir level a seasonal variable; irrigation canals as a grid of straight splines fed from the river below the dam.
generator.settlement_flattening: Plain towns and villages flattened as pads among palm groves; foothill villages on terraces; the border crossing on a flattened valley floor.
generator.notes: Palm groves give dense cover next to open fields, which shapes ambushes; the ridge gap and the dam road are the main chokepoints; the border crossing and pilgrim road carry heavy traffic. Iranian-side zones are recon and recovery only, as on iran_zagros.

settlements.architecture: Iraqi market town: two- to four-storey concrete-frame and cinder-block buildings with flat roofs, rooftop water tanks, satellite dishes and rebar stubs, shop shutters, a domed mosque and a husseiniya, a police HQ behind blast walls, and a crowded souq; some brick buildings and older mud-brick houses in the old quarter.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete frames medium; cinder-block infill thin (breachable); old mud-brick thick.
layout_rules: grid around the souq and main mosque
blast-walled police and army posts on the main road
palm groves pressing on the edges
bus station and fuel depot on the highway

settlements.architecture: Palm-grove villages: walled family compounds of cinder block and mud brick with flat roofs, orchards inside the walls, a small mosque, canal footbridges; Kurdish and Turkmen foothill villages of stone and block on terraces.
settlements.wall_class: Compound walls medium (block) or thick (mud brick); interior walls thin.
layout_rules: strung along canals inside palm groves
foothill villages stepped on slopes with a spring
mosque and shop at the crossroads

settlements.architecture: Iranian foothill border town: brick and concrete two- to four-storey buildings with flat roofs, Persian signage and murals, a bazaar street, a mosque with a tiled dome, war-memorial portraits, a Basij base and an IRGC border regiment barracks.
settlements.wall_class: Brick medium; concrete medium; shopfronts glass none.
layout_rules: bazaar street along the road from the crossing
barracks and border-regiment compound on the edge
terraced gardens on the slope above

settlements.architecture: Border crossing complex (customs halls, lorry parks, pilgrim halls, money changers, flags), ISF and Peshmerga posts with HESCO and sandbag towers, a dam with a powerhouse, oil wellpads and a gathering station, faction-held depots behind earth berms, a reservoir fish farm.
settlements.wall_class: HESCO, berms and the dam thick; prefabs, halls and tanks thin.
layout_rules: crossing in the valley on the main road with queues both sides
outposts on ridge tops and at the dam
oil field on the foothill steppe straddling the border

settlements.architecture: Pilgrim service stations (mawkibs) of tents and steel-frame sheds along the road during Arbaeen; a camp for returning displaced families; an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp on the Iraqi side.
layout_rules: mawkibs every few hundred metres on the pilgrim road (seasonal)
opposition camp in a foothill valley (strike-event target)

settlements.architecture: Orchard farms and fish ponds: a block house, a pump house, a walled orchard, a sheep pen.
settlements.wall_class: Block walls thin; mud walls medium.
layout_rules: along canals and the river below the dam

infrastructure.roads: A four-lane highway from the plain to the border crossing (the pilgrim road), a dam-crest road through the ridge gap, a road along the foothills between Kurdish and Arab districts, farm tracks and canal-bank roads, ridge tracks.
infrastructure.rail: None in service; an abandoned railway embankment on the plain.
infrastructure.power: Hydro plant at the dam, pylons on the plain, Iranian electricity imports over a cross-border line; frequent outages in summer.
infrastructure.ports: None; fishing boats on the reservoir.
infrastructure.airfields: A disused airbase on the plain used as an army helipad; Iranian side off-map.
infrastructure.checkpoints: ISF checkpoints on the highway and at the dam; Peshmerga checkpoints on the Kurdish-majority roads; faction-run checkpoints near the crossing; joint ISF-Peshmerga coordination posts in the disputed districts; Iranian border guard and IRGC posts on the east side.

conditions: winter fog in the palm groves
weather.visibility_notes: Dust storms drop visibility to under 200 m and ground aircraft; palm groves limit sight to 50-100 m; heat shimmer over the plain in summer; fog in winter mornings.
weather.dust_or_snow: Dust heavy May-September; snow only on the eastern range in winter.

civilians.behaviour: Farmers in the groves at dawn and dusk; busy souqs mornings and evenings; lorry queues at the crossing day and night; shepherds on the steppe and Hamrin slopes (cells sometimes target them); during Arbaeen, huge crowds of pilgrims on foot along the highway. Civilians avoid faction checkpoints and leave villages when ridge operations start.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Markets, the crossing and the pilgrim road are very dense; shepherds and farmers work in the same gullies and groves where cells hide. The casualty rule bites in palm-grove raids and during Arbaeen.

factions_present.where: Towns, highway and dam checkpoints, the disused airbase, ridge-top outposts on Hamrin; the border-crossing customs authority.
Kurdish-majority foothill districts in the north, the border oil field, coordination posts in the disputed districts.
Remnant cells in the Hamrin gullies and caves, the reservoir reeds and the palm groves at the gap between ISF and Peshmerga lines.
Depots and side yards near the border crossing, checkpoints on the pilgrim road, drone launch teams in orchards; shown without PMF markings (see faction notes).
Iranian side (east of the border line): IRGC border regiment posts, the foothill border town, a radar mast on the range; drone and missile events over the map and strikes on the opposition camp.

frontline: No moving front: a security-gap map. IS cells regenerate in the Hamrin gullies and the reservoir reeds; each cell zone that survives raises attacks on shepherds, checkpoints and the canal roads and posts counter-IS contracts (irq, krg_peshmerga). The disputed districts have a cooperation meter between ISF and Peshmerga: high cooperation shrinks the gap where cells live, while budget or Kirkuk-type disputes lower it. The border economy is held by iraqi_militias: their strength rises with the Iran-US/Israel war phases (drone launches at the oil field, more checkpoints) and falls with Iraqi disarmament progress. Regional-war events put Iranian drones and missiles overhead and strikes on the opposition camp, raising the alert across the map. Iranian-side zones never flip; they are recon and recovery only.

hot_zones.name: Hamrin ridge and reservoir
hot_zones.layout: isis HQ in a cave complex on the ridge; 3-5 outposts (gully hides, a reed island, an abandoned farm, a shepherd hut); ISF dam checkpoint and ridge-top outposts as friendly anchors; roaming motorbike pairs and a boat; 1 QRF cell from a palm-grove safe house

insertion.fob: FOB at the disused airbase on the plain next to (but separate from) the ISF helipad, or a Peshmerga base in the northern foothills for krg_peshmerga work. Road moves on the highway and the dam road; helicopters outside dust storms; no AAVs.

early_game_notes: isis remnant cells and iraqi_militias are early-tier; irq and krg_peshmerga are early-game clients. irn (mid tier) stays on the Iranian side and appears through strike and drone events. Captain-confirmed new theatre (2026-10-10).
